mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate, indicating monetary tightening, leads to higher borrowing costs and reduced consumer and business spending, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive (>5%) despite a 0.5% increase in FEDFUNDS over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate indicates a weak labor market, leading to reduced consumer spending and economic growth, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite high unemployment rates (>10%).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand in the housing market, which spills over into the broader economy and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite a 5% year-over-year increase in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) outpaces inflation (CPIAUCSL), it indicates a healthy economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > CPIAUCSL growth rate
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative when GDPC1 growth exceeds CPIAUCSL growth.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite an increase in INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite a 5% year-over-year increase in RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) indicates a robust labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite strong PAYEMS growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is high, it indicates a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite UNRATE increasing by > 0.5pp and FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.
